description: Returns Asset Details by given Company, Project & Asset

parameters.name: wrap_custom_fields
parameters.description: When true, wraps each custom field value as {"value": ...} and renames "name" to "label" inside LOV objects.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

schema.description: Response for single asset operations (Create, Show, Update)

asset_status.description: Reference object with id, name, and metadata (normal/extended view)

metadata.description: Additional metadata. Content varies by reference type: asset_status has status_group_id and color_code; asset_type has Asset Type ID (code in metadata) and fieldset_id; location may have parent_id.

asset_type.description: Reference object with id, name, and metadata (normal/extended view)

metadata.description: Additional metadata. Content varies by reference type: asset_status has status_group_id and color_code; asset_type has Asset Type ID (code in metadata) and fieldset_id; location may have parent_id.

location.description: Reference object with id, name, and metadata (normal/extended view)

metadata.description: Additional metadata. Content varies by reference type: asset_status has status_group_id and color_code; asset_type has Asset Type ID (code in metadata) and fieldset_id; location may have parent_id.

trade.description: Reference object with id, name, and metadata (normal/extended view)

metadata.description: Additional metadata. Content varies by reference type: asset_status has status_group_id and color_code; asset_type has Asset Type ID (code in metadata) and fieldset_id; location may have parent_id.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields as key-value pairs. Keys are field identifiers, values vary by field type.

notes.description: Notes by context. Keys: project_assignment, asset_status, etc. Exposes all context notes.

profile_image_url.description: Profile image URL. Only populated when include_profile_image=true query parameter is set.

scene_bim_object_info.description: BIM scene and object information. Populated when include_bim_info=true.

object_id.description: BIM object identifier within the scene

procore_instance_id.description: Procore instance ID for BIM object

scope.description: Scope of the asset (e.g., company, project).

attachment_count.description: Number of attachments for this asset

project.description: Reference object with id and name (compact view - no metadata)

parent_asset.description: Parent asset reference with id, name, and asset_code

id.description: Unique identifier of the parent asset

asset_code.description: Asset code of the parent asset

parent_asset_code.description: Deprecated: use parent_asset.asset_code instead. Asset code of the parent asset. Null when the asset has no parent.

punch_list.description: Number of punch list items linked to this asset

observations.description: Number of observations linked to this asset

inspections.description: Number of inspections linked to this asset

inspection_items.description: Number of inspection items linked to this asset

rfi.description: Number of RFIs linked to this asset

submittals.description: Number of submittals linked to this asset

incidents.description: Number of incidents linked to this asset

linkable.description: Whether this asset can be linked to other Procore items

has_children.description: Whether this asset has child assets

children_count.description: Number of direct child assets. Null when hasChildren is false.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
